title: Factors that affect cost, and the pricing calculator
learningObjective: Describe the factors that affect Azure costs and use the pricing calculator to estimate a solution before deploying it.
foundation: Azure bills by consumption, so what you deploy and how long it runs decides the bill.

Main cost factors: the resource type and size, how much you consume, leftover resources, the region, network traffic leaving Azure, your subscription type, and anything bought from the Azure Marketplace.

The pricing calculator (azure.microsoft.com/pricing/calculator) lets you add services, pick options and see an estimated monthly cost before you build anything. It's free and you don't need to sign in.
engineer: Resource type and size: each service, tier and SKU has its own meters. A Premium SSD costs more than Standard HDD; a D-series VM more than a B-series. Storage cost depends on type, tier, redundancy and region.

Consumption: pay-as-you-go by default; commit with reservations or savings plans for discounts. Maintenance: resources created with others (disks, NICs, public IPs, NSGs) remain after a VM is deleted unless cleaned up.

Geography: prices differ between regions because of local power, labour and tax costs. Network traffic: inbound data transfer is generally free; outbound (egress) to the internet and traffic between regions or zones is billed, in tiers by zone and volume.

Subscription type: free accounts include 12 months of popular services, credit for the first 30 days and always-free services. Azure Marketplace: third-party solutions bill their own software charges on your Azure invoice.

Pricing calculator: choose products, configure options (region, tier, billing option, support), see a per-month estimate, export or share it. Estimates aren't quotes; actual cost depends on real usage.

animation.caption: Build an estimate and compare it to a budget, then match situations to cost factors.

example.title: Estimating a new web shop
body: The team prices 2 App Service instances, an Azure SQL Database and 500 GB of outbound traffic in the calculator for two regions. North Europe is cheaper than Switzerland North for the same SKUs.
They export the estimate for the budget meeting and later notice that a forgotten test VM's disks keep costing money after the VM was deleted.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription (a free account works)
permissions: Cost Management Reader to view costs
portal: azure.microsoft.com/pricing/calculator: add products, set region and options, Export.
Cost Management > Cost analysis: compare the estimate with actual cost after deploying.
configuration.cli:
az consumption usage list --top 5 -o table
az vm list-skus -l westeurope --size Standard_D -o table

troubleshooting.symptom: Bill is much higher than the estimate.
troubleshooting.cause: Real usage (hours, egress, transactions) differs from estimate inputs.
troubleshooting.fix: Compare Cost analysis by meter with the estimate and adjust.

comparisons.difference: The calculator estimates before deploying; Cost Management tracks actual spend after.
Inbound transfer is generally free; outbound is billed.

misconceptions.myth: Azure prices are the same in every region.
Deleting a VM deletes everything it used.
misconceptions.reality: Disks, NICs and IPs may remain.

misconceptions.myth: The calculator needs an Azure subscription.
misconceptions.reality: It's free to use without signing in.

architectureDecisions: Estimate in several regions before choosing.
Design to minimise cross-region and internet egress.
